description: Policy for how much to ask per CSF subcategory. compute_scope.py works out each subcategory's STATE (a fact: GOVERN, no certification, no related control, what the SoA says about the related controls) and looks it up in `states`; `sector_bumps` then raise a few subcategories one step for the client's sector. When in doubt (a control the SoA excludes, or whose entry cannot be read) the subcategory is asked in full, with a `note` shown to the client. Change policy by editing this file, not the code.

sector_bumps.description: Subcategories asked one step more demandingly for a sector (confirmatory -> gap -> full_discovery): the areas that matter most in that sector. Maintainer judgement.

frames.gap: {cert} covers control(s) {controls}, which partially addresses this area. Beyond that coverage: {text}
frames.confirmatory: {cert} should cover control(s) {controls}. Please confirm and provide named evidence: {text}
frames.fallback_question: How does your organisation address: {outcome}? Who owns this?

no_soa.reason: {cert}: no SoA provided, OLIR mapped — assuming coverage

not_in_soa.reason: {cert}: mapped controls not in SoA (mandatory clauses only) — assuming coverage

applicable_not_implemented.reason: {control} applicable but not implemented per SoA

implementation_unknown.reason: {control} applicable but implementation status not stated in SoA — confirm with evidence

excluded.reason: {control} excluded in the SoA ({soa_reason}): asked in full, the client may answer not applicable
excluded.note: Excluded in your SoA ({control_no}: {soa_reason}). If this still does not apply, answer "Not applicable" with the reason.

unreadable.reason: {control}: the SoA's applicability ({applicable_raw}) could not be read: asked in full
unreadable.note: Your SoA's entry for {control_no} could not be read ({applicable_raw}). If this does not apply, answer "Not applicable" with the reason.

soa_reading.description: How parse_soa.py reads an ISO 27001 SoA spreadsheet. It picks the sheet, the header row and each column by these words, prints what it picked so the user can confirm, and takes --sheet / --id-col / --applicable-col / --reason-col / --implemented-col to correct a pick. A cell whose word is in neither list is read as unknown (null), never guessed.
